key_insight: A physics-constrained, data-driven reduced-order modeling approach enables efficient flapping-wing shape optimization, improving time-averaged thrust by 37% and propulsive efficiency by 40%.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce computational and memory costs for aerodynamic design involving unsteady, nonlinear flows.
method: Build physics-constrained, data-driven reduced-order models for PDE-constrained optimization.
Project optimization into system dynamics optimization in Hilbert space to improve stability.
Optimize flapping-wing geometry using the reduced-order formulation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 37% thrust and 40% efficiency improvements for a 2D flapping-wing section at Re = 2,400, plus a 3D test demonstrating potential applicability.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify computational savings or 3D performance gains, leaving scalability and broader applicability to be established.
paper_title: Aerodynamic Shape Optimization of unsteady flapping wings
